result.title: Prognosis Without Prediction: The Intrinsic Geometry of Survival
result.summary: Modeling systemic failure in high-dimensional environments is fundamentally limited by supervised algorithms that attempt to predict sparse, noisy or censored endpoints. To break this reliance on explicit outcome regression, we engineered the Self-Organizing Survival Manifolds (SOSM) framework, a deep learning architecture that decouples unsupervised representation learning from survival labels and treats time-to-event progression as an emergent geometric property. The system projects heterogeneous multi-omics arrays into a unified latent space governed by a pseudotime-weighted, curvature-minimizing graph Laplacian, organizing patient trajectories along low-dissipation geodesic flows. To validate the framework, we applied this architecture to a 184-patient clear cell renal cell carcinoma multi-omics cohort. Across a deterministic 5-fold cross-validation pipeline, SOSM achieved a mean Concordance Index of $0.768 \pm 0.068$, while out-of-fold risk stratification yielded significant survival divergence (log-rank $p < 0.001$) accompanied by a 14.7% increase in local manifold dissipation among high-risk patients. Furthermore, interrogating the network's encoder weights confirmed that the model autonomously recovered canonical metabolic and microenvironmental drivers of disease progression without supervised feature selection. By demonstrating that systemic failure can be mapped as a geometric phase transition, SOSM establishes a generalizable computational engine for prognostic modeling across biological, industrial and financial complex systems.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SOSM 框架，把多组学数据映射到统一潜空间，用伪时间加权、曲率最小化的图拉普拉斯把疾病进展组织成低耗散测地流，使生存预测成为潜空间中的涌现几何性质而非监督回归。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用测地流与局部耗散刻画潜空间状态推进的方式，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理轨迹、状态相似度与几何结构的分析提供可核查的度量思路，但任务是生存分析，与视觉推理无直接关联。
